title: Looking for expertise in AI workflow for 2D image creation. Best practices.
author: Steevo_Games
selftext:
Hello. I have about 3300 hours currently in a 2D/3D game I have been developing called Oracle Ark. I have attached some screenshots.

The game has a 2D trivia scene, where the player earns points and plays the primary trivia game, and these points are used to unlock achievements and other things in the 3D "late game" part of the story. 

I have been using chatGPT to generate initial assets, then either editing them or recreating them completely myself. This workflow has been great, but my game has a customization room, where you can unlock posters and other assets via playing trivia matches, and I'd like to have about 30 posters. 

As anyone who uses AI knows, using a chat to create 30 posters will get generic very quickly. The reality is, these tools are great, but I need some ideas on how to add some uniqueness to the unlockable images. I'm even open to not using AI at all for this. Problem is, most artists charge anywhere from $100-$1000 per image (literally) if you want to use them commercially. Multiply those numbers by 30, and you can see where my problem lies lol. Not many people can afford things like this in 2026.

So basically I'm looking for ideas on how to create a large amount of art. I'd be willing to work with people as well. Or if anyone has a specific chatGPT (or other AI) workflow that could make this viable, or just anything at all. I'm fairly open. 

I attached some screenshots of my game so people can get an idea of the art style.

comments.author: CakeData
comments.body: Just use chatgpt image generation, its pretty amazing. Work on the prompt and provide reference art and done. Might need the $20 plan, not sure.

comments.author: dasjomsyeet
comments.body:
You could train a style LoRA for a local text2image model. Since you already seem to have a good chunk of assets in the style you want, building a dataset should be straightforward.

The quality of model you’ll be able to use will depend on the power of your system. Local training will use even more than inference so if you don’t have a powerful enough rig you might still have to go with cloud services like gpt-image or nano banana.

There is also the option to rent GPU runtimes for training or inference (runpod, google colab etc). I mostly use these services because my local rig is shit but I still need open source models for finetuning and comfyui workflows.

comments.author: Effective-Caregiver8
comments.body: maybe you can look into Fiddlart and try their [Forge](https://fiddl.art/blog/en/forge-tool-train-custom-ai-models) tool.
